about.title: Personal Injury Help in Taft, California
about.longDescription: Taft may be a small city, but its roads see real traffic and real consequences. In the most recent reporting year, Kern County recorded 22 injury collisions in and around Taft, leaving 31 people hurt and 2 dead. Corridors like Rt 33, 6th Street, Kern Street, and Gardner Field Road carry much of the town's daily traffic, and collisions here tend to cluster on Saturday evenings between 7 and 9 p.m. — a pattern worth knowing whether you're a driver, a passenger, or a pedestrian. If you've been hurt in a crash or another kind of accident in Taft, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't decide or handle your case ourselves. Attorneys in our network take cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you in touch with someone who can review what happened and explain your options under California law.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Taft?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like the city or county, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months for filing a notice of claim. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total award would simply be reduced by your percentage of responsibility. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Taft?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Rt 33, 6th Street, Kern Street, and Gardner Field Road are among the higher-volume corridors for reported injury crashes in Taft. Reported crashes also tend to cluster on Saturdays between 7 and 9 p.m. These are simply public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in ordinary California personal injury cases, there's no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or emotional distress. Compensation depends on the specific facts and impact of your injury, which an attorney can help assess.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
